name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
summary: A quadruped mobility drill that increases thoracic spine rotation and upper back mobility while keeping the lumbar spine stable.

setup: Start on your hands and knees in a quadruped position with wrists directly under shoulders and knees directly under hips.
Engage your core to maintain a neutral lumbar spine.
Place one hand lightly behind your head or neck, keeping the elbow flared out to the side.
steps: Inhale as you rotate your upper torso downward, bringing the elevated elbow toward your supporting forearm.
Exhale and reverse the motion, rotating your chest and elbow upward toward the ceiling as far as comfortable without shifting your hips.
Pause briefly at the top to feel the stretch and activation through the mid and upper back.
Return smoothly to the bottom position and complete all reps before switching sides.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you rotate down toward the floor; exhale as you rotate upward and open the chest.
cues: Keep hips square to the floor.
Rotate from the mid-back, not the lower back.
Push the floor away with the supporting hand.

common_faults.fault: Shifting the hips laterally to create artificial range of motion.
common_faults.correction: Keep your hips centered and motionless over your knees; sit slightly back toward your heels if you struggle to lock your pelvis.

common_faults.fault: Cranking the neck or pulling the head with the top hand.
common_faults.correction: Rest fingertips lightly against your head and allow the head and eyes to follow the torso rotation naturally.
Actively press into the floor with the supporting palm to maintain a stable, active shoulder girdle.

precautions: Do not force end-range rotation if you experience sharp spinal or shoulder pain.
